<reason>A won by keeping the motion as written: desert studies measure dying independent papers, not firewalled public pay, and the promised reductions require a notebook officials cannot tame and neighbors will treat as shared fact. B’s vacuum weighing was forceful, but too often swapped watchdog-versus-none for the subsidy comparison and never showed public funding itself produces those reductions. A’s auditor/belief distinction and publicly funded alibi attack left B’s design story looking like a clause, not a workplace.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s R1: news-desert evidence is a different intervention, and IGs/judges unlike local journalists do not need the public to treat them as uncaptured storytellers—so a constrained subsidized beat can be a credential rather than deterrence.</best_rebuttal>
